body:
Point 1

> 13.5.1 Verify that debug modes are disabled in production environments for every component to prevent exposure of debug features and unintended information leakage.

A bit hard to read.

---

Point 2

> 13.5.2 Verify that directory browsing is disabled unless deliberately desired.

Proposal:
> 13.5.2 Verify that directory browsing is disabled in the web server configuration unless deliberately desired.

---

Point 3

> 13.5.3 Verify that the HTTP TRACE method is disabled to avoid potential information leakage.

Proposal:
> 13.5.3 Verify that usage of the HTTP TRACE method is not allowed to avoid potential information leakage.

---

Point 4

> 13.5.5 Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information and source code leakage. For example, backup files (.bak), temporary working files (.swp), compressed files (.zip, .tar.gz), and other extensions commonly used by editors must be blocked unless required.

I think the reasoning in this requirement is so year 2000. Probably I have voted to keep this requirement in the past, but maybe we should just delete it..

comments.body:
> > 13.5.1 Verify that debug modes are disabled in production environments for every component to prevent exposure of debug features and unintended information leakage.
> 
> A bit hard to read.

Agreed, how about:

_13.5.1 Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features or information leakage._

> 
> > 13.5.2 Verify that directory browsing is disabled unless deliberately desired.
> 
> Proposal:
> 
> > 13.5.2 Verify that directory browsing is disabled in the web server configuration unless deliberately desired.

+1 makes sense.

> 
> > 13.5.3 Verify that the HTTP TRACE method is disabled to avoid potential information leakage.
> 
> Proposal:
> 
> > 13.5.3 Verify that usage of the HTTP TRACE method is not allowed to avoid potential information leakage.

Small suggestion here:

_13.5.3 Verify that the HTTP TRACE method is explicitly disabled or blocked in production environments to prevent potential information leakage._

> > 13.5.5 Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information and source code leakage. For example, backup files (.bak), temporary working files (.swp), compressed files (.zip, .tar.gz), and other extensions commonly used by editors must be blocked unless required.
> 
> I think the reasoning in this requirement is so year 2000. Probably I have voted to keep this requirement in the past, but maybe we should just delete it..

I agree, I don't even think we need to bother with this in the notes.

Point 1

Jim's proposal, I changed "or" to "and"

> 13.5.1 Verify that debug modes are disabled for all components in production environments to prevent exposure of debugging features and information leakage.

---

Point 2

I think it went a bit wrong direction

I wanted to clarify what kind of directory browsing we are talking about (hence the web server configuration), but now it is asking solution, not a problem to solve. For some (Apache), it can be solved with folder-based configuration (.htaccess) as well.

~~13.5.2 Verify that directory browsing is disabled in the web server configuration unless deliberately desired.~~

---

Point 3

I don't think "disabled or blocked" is better than "is not allowed", also "explicitly disabled" is not more disabled than "disabled". I added "in production environments" to my proposal.

> 13.5.3 Verify that usage of the HTTP TRACE method is not allowed in production environments to avoid potential information leakage.

---

Point 4

Allow-listing file extensions may give some defensive effect, but I would get rid of this deprecated reasoning. We can hope that files are not edited in production anymore, at the same `git add .` may do to job and files from editors end up there.

The application should be built the way it does not need it, but... it may save a day.

> 13.5.5 Verify that the web tier is configured to serve only files with specific file extensions to prevent unintentional information, configuration, and source code leakage.

I like all of your suggestions here @elarlang and I think we are close to PR.

For 13.5.2 how about this subtle change:

_13.5.2 Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended and documented._

Is this closer to what you want to see?
Note for 13.5.2 - technically directory browsing can be also mitigated if to put just dummy index file into folder.
@elarlang and I discussed that we will use @jmanico's wording from [here](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2954#issuecomment-2802882773).

Not sure how I did not notice it during PR, but this for sure quite ironic update [proposal](https://github.com/OWASP/ASVS/issues/2954#issuecomment-2802882773) from Jim:
> 13.5.2 Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended and documented.

For this requirement, I don't think the "and documented" is necessary.

So the proposal is:
> 13.5.2 Verify that web servers do not expose directory listings to clients unless explicitly intended.
